name: Many equal-area triangles from 30 planar points
description: construct() -> exactly 30 distinct integer coordinate pairs in [-30,30]^2. Compute the absolute determinant for every triple, exclude zero-area triples, and maximize the largest multiplicity of a single positive doubled area. The local bounded integer configurations give lower constructions for positive-area multiplicity; they do not reproduce the paper's asymptotic upper-bound proof.

sources.locator: Adrian Dumitrescu, Micha Sharir, and Csaba D. Tóth, Extremal problems on triangle areas in two and three dimensions (2007). Author abstract inspected. The paper directly bounds the number of equal-area triangles determined by finite point sets. The local bounded integer configurations give lower constructions for positive-area multiplicity; they do not reproduce the paper's asymptotic upper-bound proof.

limitations: Integer coordinates are a strict restriction of arbitrary real planar configurations. Collinear triples never contribute, and a finite score is not a general extremal theorem.
Independent Python implementation; no paper text, upstream evaluator, Lean proof or prize-bank content is redistributed. Candidate Python executes as trusted research code.

state_of_the_art.statement: No documented maximum for 30 points in [-30,30]^2. Asymptotically the maximum number of equal-area triangles is between n^2 log log n (Erdős and Purdy) and O(n^(20/9)) (Raz and Sharir), Erdős Problem #1086.
